messages:
mike: heads up — noticed a perf regression on production after the latest jit+cuda graph change.

mike: symptom: tail latency for seqlen ~1024 requests jumped ~2.3x. p99 moved from 380ms -> ~880ms on our A100 fleet. :eyes:

mike: quick profiling shows runtime picked cutlass_mha_generic kernel instead of our mha_opt_v2 for those traces. not sure why autotuner switched.

anna: did autotuner logs show a different cost estimate? I thought we pinned kernel selection to arch+seqlen buckets.

sam: checking. autotuner has a new stage that includes a torch.compile warmup score. if compile traces are dynamic it prefers a generic kernel to avoid recompiles.

sam: here's the hot command I ran locally:
```
python -m perf_tool.profile --model resnet-mha --batch 1 --seqlen 1024 --device a100 

# output snippet
# kernel chosen: cutlass_mha_generic (est cost 12.6ms)
# previous best: mha_opt_v2 (measured 4.8ms)
```

rachel: that matches the production trace I pulled. The KV cache warm path is doing dynamic shape appends (kv length changes) which flips the graph shape between warmup and real run. cudagraphs captures the generic graph.

mike: so cudagraphs + torch.compile dynamic shapes -> tracer hides the specialized kernel hints, causing fallback to generic.

anna: can we detect dynamic shape variance during warmup and disable cudagraphs for that trace? We already have a flag but it's conservative. Maybe add a seqlen-skew threshold: if warmup max-seqlen / min-seqlen > 1.1 then skip graph capture.

sam: agree. Also autotuner should incorporate measured runtime (not just trace cost) after the first couple of real requests. a short live sampling policy: run 3 in-band samples on candidate kernels and switch if delta > 30%.

perf-bot: profiling hint: observed 2.1x cache miss rate increase on KV accesses around the same window — suggests KV layout/prefetcher behavior changed with cudagraphs.

rachel: interesting — cudagraphs implies different memory stride and maybe delays KV prefetch. We saw similar in the old async-batching experiment.

mike: temporary mitigation deployed: disable cudagraph capture for seqlen buckets >=512 on the A100 pool for a week. will monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy: feature-flag "cudagraph-skip-dynshape" -> rolled to eng-runtime:a100 pool (canary=10%).

anna: for long term: update kernel-selection autotuner to be architecture-aware + seq-len-aware + trace-stability-aware. weighting: measured_latency * (1 + instability_penalty).

sam: I'll add a small experiment patch: 1) during compile, mark trace as "unstable" if shapes vary. 2) signal autotuner to keep exploring specialized kernels even if trace cost higher.

rachel: also add a KV-cache warmup hook: preappend zero tokens to sim warmup traces so captured graph reflects eventual cache layout. Might reduce false negatives.

mike: sounds good. action items: @sam add autotuner patch + bench; @anna add seqlen-skew flag; @rachel PR for KV warmup hook. I'll keep the canary and collect p99 and kernel histograms.

sam: on it. I'll post perf diffs here when I have numbers.

mike: cheers — thanks all :thumbsup:
